intro: If you've been injured in an accident that wasn't your fault, you're probably looking for an accident claim solicitor near you to help you seek compensation. You want someone local who understands your situation and can guide you through the claims process. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK solicitor who handles accident claims, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for an accident claim solicitor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people in this situation need clear, local legal help to recover compensation for their injuries and losses.
needs: You were hurt in a road traffic accident and need advice on claiming for your injuries and vehicle damage.
You suffered an injury at work and want to know if you can claim compensation from your employer.
You slipped or tripped in a public place or shop and are unsure who is responsible for your injuries.
You are considering a no win, no fee arrangement but want to understand the terms and any deductions before proceeding.
You need to start a claim quickly because the three-year time limit for most injury claims is approaching.
context_heading: Key things to understand about accident claims
context: Most personal injury claims must be started within three years of the accident, so it's important not to delay. Many claims are run on a no win, no fee basis, but you should always read the terms carefully to understand any deductions from your compensation. For lower-value road traffic whiplash claims, there is a separate online portal called the Official Injury Claim portal.

Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, solicitors are regulated by the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland by the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure; if that does not resolve things, the Legal Ombudsman can look at service complaints in England and Wales.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Describe the type of accident you were involved in, such as a road traffic accident, an accident at work, or a slip or trip.
Give the date of the accident so the solicitor can check the time limit for your claim.
Explain the injuries you suffered and whether you received medical attention.
Mention any financial losses you have incurred, such as lost earnings or vehicle repair costs.
State whether you have already started a claim or spoken to another solicitor.
Confirm your location so iComply can introduce you to a solicitor near you.

faqs.q: How long do I have to make an accident claim?
faqs.a: For most personal injury claims, you must start court proceedings within three years of the accident. There are some exceptions, so it's best to get advice quickly.

faqs.q: What is no win, no fee?
faqs.a: No win, no fee means you don't pay your solicitor's fees if your claim is unsuccessful. However, you should always read the terms to understand any deductions from your compensation if you win.

faqs.q: Do I need to use the Official Injury Claim portal?
faqs.a: The Official Injury Claim portal is for lower-value road traffic whiplash claims. Your solicitor can advise whether your claim should be made through the portal or not.

faqs.q: How can I check that a solicitor is regulated?
faqs.a: In England and Wales, you can check a solicitor or firm on the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland.
